basics.name: Ruşen Birben
basics.summary: AI and Data Engineering graduate from Istanbul Technical University and independent researcher with METU’s Applied NLP Group. Research interests center on LLM reliability and evaluation, with experience in numerical precision in interpretability, Turkish LLM pre-training data, Turkish NLP benchmarks and datasets, machine unlearning, and LLM applications for finance.

experience.description:
Co-organize the [SIGTURK 2027 Shared Task](https://sigturk.github.io/workshops/2027/shared-task/) at the SIGTURK 2027 Workshop (ACL 2027) with Çağrı Toraman, Evren Ayberk Munis, and İlker Kesen. Built the Text/LLM track: 1,000 culturally grounded items in five Turkic languages (Turkish, Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Uzbek, Uyghur) across four tasks, selected from 1,750 candidates and grounded in 620 sources; wrote the evaluator, ran the baselines, and built the shared-task website.

Contribute to GemmaTurk, a 1.6B-parameter Turkish LLM: built a Turkish YouTube caption corpus (1.34M documents, 6.1B tokens), generated synthetic instruction and reasoning data, ran mid-training data-mix experiments, and run continued pre-training with long-context extension to 64K tokens.

Upcoming: TurkBench 2, an agentic extension of the TurkBench Turkish LLM benchmark, in collaboration with Turkcell.

Co-founded Fiction Studios at Bilkent Cyberpark; led technical development and coordinated three additional contributors. Built the backend of Meddah, a multilingual LLM-powered museum and tourism audio guide, and pitched it to customers and investors.

Built RAG pipelines that retrieve up-to-date context from fragmented internal sources and PDF financial reports, and agent pipelines for internal financial LLM tools. Also developed news-sentiment pipelines and web integrations at a Phillip Capital subsidiary.
Built LSTM and random-forest prototypes for log-based anomaly detection on HDFS logs for predictive maintenance; the LSTM reached 0.96 F1 and 99% accuracy on the test set.
Ran experiments on financial LLMs across sentiment analysis, tool use, reasoning, forecasting, and RAG, feeding into the Kaira capstone.

projects.title: Kaira
projects.subtitle: Undergraduate Capstone: Financial Reasoning LLM
projects.description: Fine-tuned Qwen-based LLMs with GRPO, Unsloth, and LoRA, reaching 58.08% FinQA accuracy with Qwen3-4B, up from 47.48% with Qwen2.5-3B; ran FinQA and GSM8K experiments on reward design and financial reasoning. Developed an Ollama-based chat application.

projects.title: Tobor
projects.subtitle: Autonomous Warehouse Robot
projects.description: Implemented the box pickup/drop-off mechanism for a team-built ROS2 warehouse robot with navigation and YOLO perception; contributed to data annotation.

projects.title: AIZheimer
projects.subtitle: Machine Unlearning in Stable Diffusion
projects.description: Adapted Forget-Me-Not unlearning to Stable Diffusion 2.1, implementing attention controllers and testing loss objectives to erase target concepts while preserving unrelated generation.

projects.title: Biting The Bytes
projects.subtitle: Turkish Diacritic Restoration
projects.description: Led ByT5-small fine-tuning with PEFT/LoRA for byte-level Turkish diacritic restoration, reaching 96.18% word-level accuracy on the test set and tying for 2nd of 17 teams in the course's Kaggle competition; co-deployed the model on Hugging Face Spaces.

projects.title: To-AI-or-Not-to-AI
projects.subtitle: GPT Detector
projects.description: Built an ensemble of three fine-tuned RoBERTa detectors combined by majority vote, reaching 94.21% accuracy on the held-out test split of a 26,270-example dataset prepared with teammates.

publications.title: Patching Fails Small, Attribution Fails Large: Component Effects in 16-Bit Language Models
publications.subtitle: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) - Under review
publications.description:
Sole author.

Shows across ten language models that bfloat16 puts an error floor under intervention-based interpretability effects, while attribution keeps the ranking and sign of single-neuron effects (rank correlation ≥ 0.97); recommends measuring the floor before trusting 16-bit interventions.

publications.title: Tokenization Strategies for Pretraining Generative Large Language Models: A Case Study in Turkish
publications.subtitle: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research (JAIR) - Under review
publications.description:
Evren Ayberk Munis and **Ruşen Birben** (equal contribution, joint first authors), Çağrı Toraman.

Compared eight lossless tokenizers, including morpheme-constrained BPE, for Turkish LLM pretraining on a fixed 30 GB budget: bits per byte differed by at most 1.2%, while estimated training compute differed by up to 49%; morpheme-constrained BPE cost 23 to 29% more compute than byte-level BPE.

publications.title: Exact First, Then Fast: An Event-for-Event C++ Rebuild of the Agenthon ABIDES Market
publications.subtitle: Agenthon Workshop @ [NeurIPS 2026](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026) - In-person poster, Atlanta, USA, December 12, 2026
publications.description:
Göktürk Batın Dervişoğlu, Muhammed Faruk Aytin, **Muhammed Rüşen Birben**.

Rebuilt the Agenthon ABIDES market simulator in C++, preserving event ordering, random-number sequences, and reference outputs. Validated exact agreement across 6,900 randomized comparisons and achieved a 1,299× simulation-loop speedup on the largest public benchmark.

publications.title: Turkish Cultural Knowledge Dataset
publications.subtitle: MRL Workshop @ [EMNLP 2026](https://2026.emnlp.org/) - Dataset accepted; joint paper in preparation
publications.description:
Led the source-grounded agent pipeline and data preparation for a Turkish cultural knowledge dataset spanning 15 domains.

Generated 1,200 candidate question-answer pairs with 15 domain agents, selected 500 for sociological review by Büşra Tufan (who chose the final 300), and prepared the submission.

Reviewed English translations; supervised by Çağrı Toraman.
